title: ～直す — do ～ over again
summary: Attached to the stem of a verb, 直す means “do it over again, redo it (to fix or improve it).” It is used when something was wrong or unsatisfactory and you do it again from scratch.

patterns.gloss: verb stem + 直す: redo (書く → 書き直す)

body.p: 直す on its own means “to correct.” Added to the stem of a verb, it forms compound verbs meaning to redo the action, such as 書き直す, 言い直す and 考え直す.

Use it to fix a mistake, to make something better, or to reconsider. 考え直す means to rethink and reach a new decision. Compared with simply saying “do it once more,” 直す carries the feeling of wanting to improve on the first time.

examples.ja: 間違（まちが）えたので、書（か）き直（なお）しました。
examples.tr: I made a mistake, so I rewrote it.

examples.ja: 発音（はつおん）が悪（わる）かったので、もう一度（いちど）言（い）い直（なお）した。
examples.romaji: Hatsuon ga warukatta node, mō ichido iinaoshita.
examples.tr: My pronunciation was bad, so I said it over once more.
examples.note: 言う → 言い直す: to say it again correctly.

examples.ja: 計画（けいかく）を最初（さいしょ）から考（かんが）え直（なお）すことにした。
examples.romaji: Keikaku o saisho kara kangaenaosu koto ni shita.
examples.tr: I decided to rethink the plan from the very start.
examples.note: 考える → 考え直す: to reconsider.

pitfalls: Attach it to the verb stem: 書き直す, not 書いて直す.
Do not confuse it with 治す (cure an illness). The suffix 〜直す means redoing.
